newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa examines exchange control tax issues.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa examines exchange control tax issues.

text.p: The South African Revenue Services is considering how to provide tax clearance to individuals by July 1, Commissioner Trevor van Heerden said on Tuesday.

He told the parliamentary finance committee the SARS had been investigating this since Finance Minister Trevor Manuel announced in his March budget that only individuals "in good standing" with tax officials would be able to transfer money into foreign bank accounts.

"This is one of the measures that is being taken to ensure that the tax base is broadened. The other one is the greater use of the tax number and the ID number throughout the banking system," he said. "We have been concerned right from the beginning that we should not delay the transfer of money or be a burden on the system."

The SARS had therefore considered including a document in applications to take money out of the country. This would be processed by SARS officials. But the problem was that the SARS was in the throes of updating its systems and did not have any idea of how many forms it would have to process.

"So we initially see it as being a process where a declaration will be made up front and we will then process that declaration," he said. "As soon as our systems are in place, we would then want to change over to the next process of issuing the certificates applied for."
This would not affect holiday travel allowances.
By good standing, the SARS believed that taxpayers' returns would have to be up to date and outstanding tax either paid or arrangements made to pay it.

Volumes handled would also be affected by the fact that the Tender Board was also starting to grant contracts to companies and individuals in good standing with the SARS, while some Department of Trade and Industry support programmes depended on tax clearance as well.
